title: The cohomology pullback is induced by the unit of the derived adjunction
statement:
Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $u_*$ be the direct image and $Ru_*:\Dplus(Y_{\Et})\to\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $Ru_*L=u_*J$ for a K-injective resolution $L\to J$, its derived functor [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], let $u^{-1}:\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ be the inverse image on bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $\eta^D_u:\mathrm{id}\to Ru_*u^{-1}$ be the unit of the derived adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. Write $\RGamma(T_{\Et},-)$ and $H^q(T_{\Et},-)$ for the derived global sections and the cohomology groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then:

1. (Leray identification.) For every bounded below K-injective complex $J$ of abelian sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$, the complex $u_*J$ on $X_{\Et}$ is K-injective; hence for $L\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ with K-injective resolution $L\to J$ the equality of complexes $\Gamma(X,u_*J)=\Gamma(Y,J)$ (as $(u_*J^r)(X)=J^r(X\times_XY)=J^r(Y)$) is an isomorphism $\lambda_L:\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ru_*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},L)$ in $\Dplus(\Ab)$, natural in $L$.
2. (Alternative description of $u^*$.) For every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, in particular for an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ placed in degree $0$, the pullback $u^*:\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] equals the composite

$$
 \RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\xrightarrow{\ \RGamma(X,\eta^D_{u,K})\ }\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ru_*u^{-1}K)\xrightarrow{\ \lambda_{u^{-1}K}\ }\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K),
$$

and so $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of this composite for every $q\ge0$. Here $\RGamma(T_{\Et},-)$ acts on morphisms as the derived functor of the additive left exact functor $\Gamma(T,-)$ on $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] (for $a:K\to K'$, $\RGamma(T,a)$ is the class of $\Gamma(T,\tilde a)$, $\tilde a$ the unique homotopy class of maps of the chosen K-injective resolutions lifting $a$), and a complex $\Gamma(T,I)$ computed from any K-injective complex $I$ with an isomorphism $QI\cong K$ is identified with $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)$ by the canonical isomorphism $Q\Gamma(T,h)$, $h$ the comparison homotopy equivalence of resolutions; the equalities of clauses 1 and 2 are meant after these identifications, which are the ones of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (1).

proof.text: *Conventions: $\Gamma$, $u_*$ and their derived functors.* For a scheme $T$, $\Gamma(T,-):\Ab(T_{\Et})\to\Ab$ is evaluation at the final object $T$ of $T_{\Et}$; it is additive (sums of sheaf maps are computed sectionwise) and left exact (kernels of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise), and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is a Grothendieck abelian category with enough injectives [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. So [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] applies to $v=\Gamma(T,-)$ and to $v=u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: for $K\in\Dplus$ with chosen K-injective resolution $\rho_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI(K)$ ($I(K)=\operatorname{Kinj}(K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $Q$ the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), $RvK=Q(v\,I(K))$, so $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=Q\Gamma(T,I(K))$ and $Ru_*K=Q(u_*I(K))$; and for $a:K\to K'$, $Rv(a)=Q(v(\tilde a))$ where $\tilde a:I(K)\to I(K')$ is the unique homotopy class with $Q(\tilde a)\rho_K=\rho_{K'}a$, which exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $I(K')$ being K-injective. Since $v$ is additive, it carries homotopic maps to homotopic maps, so $v(\tilde a)$ is well defined up to homotopy.

proof.text: *Computation on arbitrary K-injective representatives.* Let $v$ be $\Gamma(T,-)$ or $u_*$ (step 1). For $K\in\Dplus$ call a pair $(I,\sigma)$ with $I$ a K-injective complex and $\sigma:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ an isomorphism a *representative* of $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] there is a unique homotopy class $h_\sigma:I\to I(K)$ with $Q(h_\sigma)=\rho_K\sigma^{-1}$; it is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence (last sentence of that node), so $v(h_\sigma)$ is a homotopy equivalence ($v$ additive) and $\tau_\sigma:=Q(v(h_\sigma)):Q(vI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RvK$ is an isomorphism; for $(I,\sigma)=(I(K),\rho_K)$, $h=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tau=\mathrm{id}$. Claim: if $(I,\sigma)$, $(I',\sigma')$ represent $K$, $K'$, $a:K\to K'$, and $f:I\to I'$ is a morphism of complexes with $Q(f)\sigma=\sigma'a$, then $Rv(a)\circ\tau_\sigma=\tau_{\sigma'}\circ Q(v(f))$. Proof: $\tilde a h_\sigma$ and $h_{\sigma'}f$ are maps $I\to I(K')$ with $Q(\tilde a h_\sigma)=\rho_{K'}a\sigma^{-1}$ and $Q(h_{\sigma'}f)=\rho_{K'}\sigma'^{-1}Q(f)=\rho_{K'}\sigma'^{-1}\sigma'a\sigma^{-1}=\rho_{K'}a\sigma^{-1}$; by the injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] ($I(K')$ K-injective) $\tilde a h_\sigma\simeq h_{\sigma'}f$; applying the additive $v$ and then $Q$ gives $Q(v\tilde a)\,Q(vh_\sigma)=Q(vh_{\sigma'})\,Q(vf)$, the claim (step 1: $Rv(a)=Q(v\tilde a)$). Special case $a=\mathrm{id}_K$: for two representatives of one $K$ and $f$ with $Q(f)\sigma=\sigma'$, $\tau_\sigma=\tau_{\sigma'}\circ Q(v(f))$; these $\tau$ are the canonical identifications between complexes computed from different resolutions (the maps $\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi)$ for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], step 1(a) and clause 1).

proof.text: *Clause 1, K-injectivity of $u_*J$.* The inverse image $u^{-1}:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and left adjoint to $u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; $u_*$ is additive (on sections, $(u_*\varphi)_W=\varphi_{W\times_XY}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]). By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] (with $u=u_*$, $v=u^{-1}$; its notion of K-injective is that of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], as recorded there) the termwise complex $u_*J$ is K-injective for every K-injective complex $J$ on $Y_{\Et}$ (Stacks' proof: for acyclic $M$, $u^{-1}M$ is acyclic, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(M,u_*J)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(u^{-1}M,J)=0$); if $J$ is bounded below so is $u_*J$, as $u_*0=0$.

proof.text: *Clause 1, the isomorphism $\lambda_L$.* Let $L\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ and let $(J,\sigma)$ be a representative of $L$ (step 2), e.g. $(I(L),\rho_L)$. The equality of complexes $e_J:\Gamma(X,u_*J)=\Gamma(Y,J)$ holds termwise, $(u_*J^r)(X)=J^r(X\times_XY)=J^r(Y)$, and on differentials, $(u_*d^r)_X=d^r_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (the identification $X\times_XY=Y$ being the canonical one). Let $c:J\to I(L)$ be the homotopy class with $Q(c)\sigma=\rho_L$ (it is $h_\sigma$ of step 2, a homotopy equivalence). Then $u_*J$ is K-injective (step 3) and $\sigma_*:=Q(u_*c)^{-1}:Ru_*L=Q(u_*I(L))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u_*J)$ makes $(u_*J,\sigma_*)$ a representative of $Ru_*L$ ($Q(u_*c)$ is invertible, $u_*c$ being a homotopy equivalence). Define $\lambda_L=\tau^{Y}_{\sigma}\circ Q(e_J)\circ(\tau^{X}_{\sigma_*})^{-1}:\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ru_*L)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},L)$, with $\tau^X$, $\tau^Y$ the isomorphisms of step 2 for $v=\Gamma(X,-)$ on $Ru_*L$ and $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$ on $L$; it is a composite of isomorphisms of $\Dplus(\Ab)$. Independence of $(J,\sigma)$: comparing with $(I(L),\rho_L)$, step 2 (case $a=\mathrm{id}$, $f=c$, resp. $f=u_*c$ from $(u_*J,\sigma_*)$ to $(u_*I(L),\mathrm{id})$, since $Q(u_*c)\sigma_*=\mathrm{id}$) gives $\tau^Y_\sigma=\tau^Y_{\rho_L}Q(\Gamma(Y,c))$ and $\tau^X_{\sigma_*}=\tau^X_{\mathrm{id}}Q(\Gamma(X,u_*c))$, and $e_{I(L)}\circ\Gamma(X,u_*c)=\Gamma(Y,c)\circ e_J$ because $(u_*c)_X=c_Y$; so both choices give the same $\lambda_L$. In particular, for the chosen resolution, $\lambda_L=\tau^X_{\mathrm{id}}$-conjugate of the literal equality $\Gamma(X,u_*I(L))=\Gamma(Y,I(L))$, which is the statement of clause 1.

proof.text: *Clause 1, naturality of $\lambda$.* Let $b:L\to L'$ in $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$, $J=I(L)$, $J'=I(L')$, and $\tilde b:J\to J'$ the lift of step 1, so $Ru_*(b)=Q(u_*\tilde b)$. Step 2 for $v=\Gamma(X,-)$, $a=Ru_*(b)$, representatives $(u_*J,\mathrm{id})$, $(u_*J',\mathrm{id})$ and $f=u_*\tilde b$ (indeed $Q(u_*\tilde b)\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\circ Ru_*(b)$) gives $\RGamma(X,Ru_*b)\circ\tau^X=\tau'^X\circ Q(\Gamma(X,u_*\tilde b))$; step 2 for $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$, $a=b$, $f=\tilde b$ gives $\RGamma(Y,b)\circ\tau^Y=\tau'^Y\circ Q(\Gamma(Y,\tilde b))$ (here all $\tau=\mathrm{id}$ for the chosen resolutions, but the computation is the same for any representatives); and $e_{J'}\circ\Gamma(X,u_*\tilde b)=\Gamma(Y,\tilde b)\circ e_J$ since $(u_*\tilde b)_X=\tilde b_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Combining, $\lambda_{L'}\circ\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ru_*b)=\RGamma(Y_{\Et},b)\circ\lambda_L$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray): the commutative diagram of functors $R\Gamma(X,-)\circ Rf_*=R\Gamma(Y,-)$; naturality written out by the agent

proof.text: *Clause 2, a representative of the derived unit.* Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ be represented as in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]: a bounded below complex $K^\bullet$ with $\kappa:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QK^\bullet$, a K-injective resolution $s:K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ and a K-injective resolution $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ on $Y_{\Et}$. Since $u^{-1}$ is exact, $u^{-1}(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $r\circ u^{-1}(s):u^{-1}K^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution of the bounded below complex $u^{-1}K^\bullet$, which represents $u^{-1}(QK^\bullet)$ through $\varphi_{K^\bullet}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Property (2) of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction] with $M=K^\bullet$ and this resolution says: $\eta^D_{u,QK^\bullet}$ is the class of $K^\bullet\xrightarrow{\eta_{u,K^\bullet}}u_*u^{-1}K^\bullet\xrightarrow{u_*(r\,u^{-1}s)}u_*J^\bullet$, under the identification $Q(u_*J^\bullet)\cong Ru_*u^{-1}QK^\bullet$ of that node, i.e. with $\sigma_*:Ru_*u^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u_*J^\bullet)$ the isomorphism making $(u_*J^\bullet,\sigma_*)$ a representative as in step 4 (transported along $\kappa$ by naturality of $\eta^D$). Naturality of the unit $\eta_u$ of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] applied to $s$ gives $u_*u^{-1}(s)\circ\eta_{u,K^\bullet}=\eta_{u,I^\bullet}\circ s$, so this morphism equals $f\circ s$ with $f:=u_*(r)\circ\eta_{u,I^\bullet}:I^\bullet\to u_*J^\bullet$. Hence, with $\sigma:=Q(s)\kappa:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI^\bullet$ (a representative of $K$, $I^\bullet$ K-injective), $\sigma_*\circ\eta^D_{u,K}=Q(f)\circ\sigma$, and $u_*J^\bullet$ is K-injective (step 3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01F8 (lemma-functoriality) and its proof, applied to $\mathcal G^\bullet=K^\bullet$, $\mathcal F^\bullet=u^{-1}K^\bullet$, $\varphi=\eta_{u,K^\bullet}$: the map $\mathcal G^\bullet\to f_*\mathcal F^\bullet\to f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$

proof.text: *Clause 2, the comparison.* Apply step 2 with $v=\Gamma(X,-)$, $a=\eta^D_{u,K}:K\to Ru_*u^{-1}K$, representatives $(I^\bullet,\sigma)$ and $(u_*J^\bullet,\sigma_*)$ and the morphism $f$ of step 6: $\RGamma(X,\eta^D_{u,K})\circ\tau^X_\sigma=\tau^X_{\sigma_*}\circ Q(\Gamma(X,f))$. By step 4 (with $L=u^{-1}K$ and the representative $(J^\bullet,\sigma')$, $\sigma'$ the isomorphism $u^{-1}K\cong QJ^\bullet$ given by $Q(r\,u^{-1}s)\varphi_{K^\bullet}u^{-1}(\kappa)$, whose $\sigma_*$ is the one of step 6), $\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\tau^X_{\sigma_*}=\tau^Y_{\sigma'}\circ Q(e_{J^\bullet})$. Hence $\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_{u,K})\circ\tau^X_\sigma=\tau^Y_{\sigma'}\circ Q(e_{J^\bullet}\circ\Gamma(X,f))$. On a section $a\in I^r(X)$: $\Gamma(X,f)(a)=(u_*r)_X(\eta_{u,I^r}(a))=r_Y(\eta_{u,I^r}(a))$, an element of $\Gamma(X,u_*J^r)=J^r(Y)$; so $e_{J^\bullet}\circ\Gamma(X,f)$ is literally the morphism of complexes $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,J^\bullet)$, $a\mapsto r(\eta_u(a))$, whose class is $u^*$ in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. The isomorphisms $\tau^X_\sigma:Q\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)$ and $\tau^Y_{\sigma'}:Q\Gamma(Y,J^\bullet)\cong\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$ are the canonical identifications under which that definition reads $u^*$ as a morphism $\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$ (step 2, last sentence; [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] clause 1 for independence of $I^\bullet,J^\bullet$). So $u^*=\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(X_{\Et},\eta^D_{u,K})$, which is clause 2 for complexes.

proof.text: *Clause 2 on cohomology groups.* Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ and $K=QG[0]$, so $K^\bullet=G[0]$, $u^{-1}K^\bullet=(u^{-1}G)[0]$ and $u^{-1}K=Q((u^{-1}G)[0])$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. The cohomology functors $\mathcal H^q$ on $\Dplus(\Ab)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^q(Q(g))=\mathcal H^q(g)$ for a morphism of complexes $g$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By step 7, $\mathcal H^q(\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_{u,K}))=\mathcal H^q(\tau^Y_{\sigma'})\circ\mathcal H^q(a\mapsto r(\eta_u(a)))\circ\mathcal H^q(\tau^X_\sigma)^{-1}$; the middle map is $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (groups $\mathcal H^q\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$, $\mathcal H^q\Gamma(Y,J^\bullet)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]), and $\mathcal H^q(\tau)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,h))$ are the identifications $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ of the groups computed from different resolutions [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent], [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. Hence $u^*$ on $H^q$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the composite, for every $q\ge0$.
